objects.original: Borel measurable real coefficient f and one globally smooth real approximant g.
objects.reconstructed: f:R->R and existential g with ContDiff R infinity g.
objects.evidence: The real codomain identifies the norm with absolute value; ContDiff at infinity means smoothness on all R.

domains.original: Closed finite interval [a,b], a<=b; restricted Lebesgue integrals.
domains.reconstructed: Set.Icc a b and volume.restrict (Icc a b).
domains.evidence: No oriented interval integral occurs. Global smoothness is distinct from the pointwise bounds restricted to Icc.

quantifiers.original: For every admissible a,b,C,epsilon,f there exists one g satisfying all three conclusions.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Universal binders followed by one existential g and conjunction of smoothness, range, error.
quantifiers.evidence: The same witness w=v+delta is returned once; no interval or tolerance is fixed universally after witness choice.

assumptions.original: C>=0, epsilon>0, a<=b, f Borel measurable, range [0,C] almost everywhere on [a,b].
assumptions.reconstructed: hab, hC, hε, Measurable f, restricted-volume a.e. membership in Icc 0 C.
assumptions.evidence: Every source hypothesis is present; no positive lower bound on f, positive interval length, or pointwise range premise is added.

conclusion.original: g globally smooth, 0<g<=C+epsilon at every interval point, integral absolute error <epsilon.
conclusion.reconstructed: ContDiff plus universal interval range and set integral norm error <epsilon.
conclusion.evidence: Real.norm_eq_abs and the single returned witness identify the conclusion exactly.

scopes.original: Includes a=b and C=0; arbitrary exceptional and outside-interval values of f.
scopes.reconstructed: No exclusion of zero length or zero C; range assumption is only restricted a.e.
scopes.evidence: hδ uses L+1, not L; hν transfers membership a.e.; source audit boundary cases are retained.

constant_dependencies.original: g may depend on f,a,b,C,epsilon; delta=epsilon/(4*(b-a+1)).
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Same delta; continuous approximation uses epsilon/2 and smoothing uses delta/2.
constant_dependencies.evidence: hδEq and hδL prove 2*delta*(b-a)<epsilon/2. No unidentified extra smallness assumption occurs.
